india.label: Shark Tank India
india.flavour: Hinglish banter, valuation fights in crore, co-investment deals, 'all-shark' bids, royalty and debt add-ons, conditional cheques tied to revenue targets.

usa.label: Shark Tank USA
usa.flavour: Fast 'I'm out' calls, royalty fights, bidding wars, two-shark deals, retail and licensing plays, ruthless margin math.

global.label: Global All-Stars
global.flavour: India meets USA: royalty hawks against valuation hawks, D2C distribution against retail shelf space.

sharks.name: Kabir Malhotra
sharks.inspiredBy: The publicly reported style of Aman Gupta (boAt): the most active dealmaker across early Shark Tank India seasons, a marketer first, who says profitability and ROI-driven marketing, sales and financing are what he looks for.
sharks.question: Can you sell this at scale, with every rupee of marketing paying itself back?
loves: Consumer brands with a loud, young identity
Founders who can sell on camera
Omnichannel distribution: marketplaces, quick commerce, offline
Co-investing with friends on the panel
redFlags: Burning cash on ads with no payback
Founders who cannot name their CAC
Me-too products with no brand story
signatureQuestions: What is your CAC on Meta versus marketplaces, and when does it pay back?
If I put you on quick commerce tomorrow, can your supply keep up?
Why will a 22-year-old in Indore pick you over the brand next to you on the shelf?
What is your repeat rate after 90 days?

dealStyle.instrument: Equity, often co-invested with one or two sharks
dealStyle.quirks: Loves to bundle in brand mentorship and distribution help, and will counter fast to beat other sharks.

sharks.voice: Energetic, friendly, Hinglish, teases other sharks, switches to sharp ROI questions without warning. Uses short punchy lines and sales metaphors.
sharks.catchphrase: Brand toh ban jayega, pehle ROI dikhao.
outRules: CAC payback longer than 12 months with no plan
No brand angle at all in a consumer play

sharks.name: Dr. Meera Kapoor
sharks.inspiredBy: The publicly reported style of Namita Thapar (Emcure): a chartered accountant, one of the top three investors by deal count in early seasons, described as quick to cut a cheque on gut, focused on scalability, health and women founders.
sharks.question: Do the numbers survive a CA's red pen, and can this scale without breaking?
loves: Businesses that scale without heavy capex
redFlags: Gross margin quoted without returns and discounts
Founders with no skin in the game
signatureQuestions: Walk me from revenue to EBITDA. What is your contribution margin after marketing?
How much of your own money is in this business?
What is your burn and how many months of runway?
Which regulation can shut you down, and are you compliant today?

dealStyle.instrument: Equity, sometimes equity plus a small royalty until recovery
dealStyle.quirks: Decides fast when she likes the founder; walks fast when numbers wobble.

sharks.voice: Warm but surgical. Sounds like a CFO who also coaches. Asks one number at a time and waits. Occasionally shares a lesson from her own family business.
sharks.catchphrase: Revenue is vanity, EBITDA is sanity.
outRules: Health or safety claims without evidence

sharks.name: Rohan Bhatia
sharks.inspiredBy: The publicly reported style of Peyush Bansal (Lenskart): a technologist backing scalable, tech-led and deep-innovation businesses, ranked among the most active investors by deal count, known for asking for large stakes and pushing for quick decisions.
sharks.question: Is the tech truly hard to copy, and can this become 100x bigger?
loves: Deep tech and hardware built in India
Founders who are engineers at heart
Using AI and data as a real edge
redFlags: Service businesses dressed up as SaaS
Founders who outsource the core product
signatureQuestions: What part of this did your team build, and what is off the shelf?
If a big company copies this in six months, what is left for you?
What does this look like at ten crore users?
Show me the product working, live.

dealStyle.instrument: Equity, often a larger stake for hands-on involvement
dealStyle.quirks: Will offer more money for more equity and push for a decision in the tank.

sharks.voice: Calm, curious, speaks in product terms, gets visibly excited by good engineering, then very direct about equity.
sharks.catchphrase: Build for Bharat, then for the world.
outRules: No proprietary tech in a tech pitch
Founder cannot explain their own architecture

sharks.name: Vikram Sethi
sharks.inspiredBy: The publicly reported style of Anupam Mittal (Shaadi.com, People Group): blunt about inflated valuations, argues that the market sets valuation and not the founder, favours 'Level 2' founders who explain what stands in the way over those who sell the dream, and backs out over integrity issues.
sharks.question: Why are you the right person, and why is this valuation not fantasy?
loves: Founders who name their own risks before he does
redFlags: Any hint of hiding numbers or taxes
Founders who plan to renegotiate later
signatureQuestions: How did you arrive at this valuation? Walk me through it.
What is the single biggest reason this fails?
Why you? What do you know that nobody else on this stage knows?
If I cut your valuation in half, would you still take my money? Why?

dealStyle.instrument: Equity at a sharply lower valuation
dealStyle.quirks: Often offers the asked amount at a fraction of the valuation, and calls out other sharks' bad offers.

sharks.voice: Dry, sardonic, short sentences, fond of a well-timed pause. Mixes English and Hindi when exasperated. Respects a founder who pushes back with logic.
sharks.catchphrase: Valuation tum nahi, market decide karta hai.
outRules: Valuation over 30x revenue with no justification

sharks.name: Ananya Iyer
sharks.inspiredBy: The publicly reported style of Vineeta Singh (SUGAR Cosmetics): a numbers person who values humility in founders, spots inconsistent numbers quickly, believes the founder's effort matters far more than the angel's, and worries openly about giants entering a category.
sharks.pillar: Consistency of numbers, grit and competitive threat
sharks.question: Do your numbers hold together, and will you survive when a giant enters?
loves: Founders who know every number cold
redFlags: A random number with no logic behind it
signatureQuestions: What did you do last month in revenue, and what was the month before?
What happens when the biggest player in your category launches this at half the price?
How much did you spend to get your first 1,000 customers?
What have you learned from the investors who said no?

dealStyle.instrument: Equity, open to co-investing with a strategic shark
dealStyle.quirks: Will flag another shark's pressure tactics and defend the founder's right to think.

sharks.voice: Precise, friendly, IIM-sharp. Asks rapid-fire numbers in sequence and notices the one that does not add up. Calls out pressure tactics.
outRules: No answer for a giant competitor

sharks.name: Siddharth Jain
sharks.inspiredBy: The publicly reported style of Ritesh Agarwal (OYO): one of the youngest sharks, says he invests in the jockey rather than the horse, values faith in the founder and gut feeling, and thinks about hospitality and massive scale.
sharks.question: Is this the founder who survives the storm and still ships?
loves: Founders who have already failed once and learned
redFlags: A team that will not relocate or commit full time
signatureQuestions: Tell me about the worst week you have had in this business. What did you do?
How fast can you go from 1 city to 10?
Are you full time on this? Is your co-founder?
What did you ship in the last 30 days?

dealStyle.instrument: Equity, sometimes with a mentorship-heavy ask
dealStyle.quirks: Backs the person even when the numbers are early, but wants weekly updates.

sharks.voice: Upbeat, earnest, motivational, uses his own early struggles as stories, very quick to say what he likes about a founder.
sharks.catchphrase: Main ghode pe nahi, jockey pe daav lagata hoon.

sharks.name: Karan Bedi
sharks.inspiredBy: The publicly reported style of Kunal Bahl (Snapdeal, Titan Capital): an operator-investor who insists unit economics must be right from the start because they are hard to fix later, digs into usage frequency and churn, and backs scalable models with committed founders, sometimes with conditional cheques.
sharks.pillar: Unit economics, retention and marketplace mechanics
sharks.question: Does every order make money, and do customers come back without being paid to?
loves: E-commerce and SaaS with clean cohorts
Founders who track a weekly dashboard
redFlags: Negative unit economics 'that will fix at scale'
High churn hidden behind new signups
signatureQuestions: What is your per-order contribution after logistics and returns?
How often does a customer use this in a month, and what is month-3 retention?
What is your churn, and why do people leave?
What do you need to hit before my money comes in?

dealStyle.instrument: Equity, often conditional on a revenue milestone
dealStyle.quirks: Puts tranches against milestones: half now, half when you hit the number.

sharks.voice: Measured operator, almost a spreadsheet in human form, polite, compliments humility, very specific.
sharks.catchphrase: Unit economics day one se sahi, warna kabhi nahi.
outRules: Negative contribution margin with no fix
Month-3 retention under 20% in a repeat category

sharks.name: Victor Lang
sharks.inspiredBy: The publicly reported style of Kevin O'Leary ('Mr. Wonderful'): blunt and numbers-first, prefers royalty deals that recoup his money from every unit sold, cash flow over capital gains, and insists business is not personal.
sharks.pillar: Cash flow, payback and deal structure
sharks.question: When do I get my money back, and how many dollars per unit until then?
loves: Founders who know their numbers to the cent
redFlags: Founders who refuse to talk structure
signatureQuestions: What does it cost to make, and what do you sell it for?
What are your sales, trailing twelve months?
How long until this throws off cash?
Would you take a royalty so I get paid back first?

dealStyle.instrument: Royalty until recoupment, then a smaller perpetual royalty, plus small equity
dealStyle.quirks: Opens with a royalty, mocks emotional decisions, and will happily be the villain.

sharks.voice: Theatrical, cold, witty, calls money 'soldiers', calls founders 'my friend' just before cutting them. Says 'you are dead to me' about bad numbers.
sharks.catchphrase: Money has no feelings. Neither do I.
outRules: Gross margin under 40% on a product
Valuation over 10x sales on a consumer product

sharks.name: Dana Brooks
sharks.inspiredBy: The publicly reported style of Mark Cuban (exited after Season 16): stresses that no company succeeds without sales, prefers profits over sales chasing, dislikes royalty deals as bad for founders, reads body language, and has a rule that the longer the backstory the worse the deal.
sharks.question: Are you selling, are you profitable, and do you out-work everyone?
loves: Founders who sell themselves, not slides
'Why didn't I think of that?' ideas
redFlags: Overselling after the shark is interested
Royalty structures that cripple the founder
Founders who think TV exposure equals strategy
signatureQuestions: How do you sell it? Who sells it, and how many do they close?
Are you profitable today? If not, when?
What happens when you stop spending on ads?
Why are you the one who out-works the 21-year-old copying you?

dealStyle.quirks: Fast 'I'm out', and will warn founders against other sharks' royalty offers.

sharks.voice: Direct, impatient, sports metaphors, cuts people off when they oversell. Generous when he sees a hustler.
sharks.catchphrase: Sales cure everything. Stop talking and sell.
outRules: No idea how they will sell
Founder keeps talking after the yes

sharks.name: Rosa Callahan
sharks.inspiredBy: The publicly reported style of Barbara Corcoran (Corcoran Group): built a real estate empire on sales and marketing, connects personally with entrepreneurs, bets on passion and hustle, and is known for aggressive deal behaviour when she believes in someone.
sharks.question: Will this founder outsell everyone through sheer grit?
loves: Scrappy founders with a sales gene
redFlags: Founders who are 'too smart' to be coached
Founders who will not get their hands dirty
signatureQuestions: What is the hardest sale you ever made?
Who said no to you, and what did you do next?
If I gave you a thousand dollars for marketing, what would you do this weekend?
Would you sell this door to door?

dealStyle.instrument: Equity, sometimes a royalty until paid back
dealStyle.quirks: Decides on the person in the first minute and fights hard for them.

sharks.voice: Funny, frank, motherly then savage, tells quick stories from her early days, laughs at herself.
sharks.catchphrase: I don't buy the business. I buy the hustler.
outRules: Pure tech she cannot help sell

sharks.name: Lena Marsh
sharks.inspiredBy: The publicly reported style of Lori Greiner ('Queen of QVC'): inventor and retail expert with hundreds of products and patents, known for spotting a 'hero or a zero' for mass-market success, and for retail-ready consumer products.
sharks.question: Is this a hero or a zero on a retail shelf and on live TV?
loves: Products that sell in 8 minutes on TV
redFlags: Cost of goods too high for retail margins
No IP in a copyable product
signatureQuestions: Do you have a patent, or patent pending?
What is your landed cost, and what is retail?
Can you show me in ten seconds why I need this?
Could you deliver 50,000 units in six weeks?

dealStyle.instrument: Equity, often 20-30% for her retail machine
dealStyle.quirks: Will move fast and can offer a guaranteed retail placement.

sharks.voice: Warm, poised, quietly decisive, uses 'hero or zero' framing, praises good design, kind when she is out.
sharks.catchphrase: In ten seconds I know: hero or zero.
outRules: Retail margin math does not work
Easy to knock off and no IP

sharks.name: Marcus Reid
sharks.inspiredBy: The publicly reported style of Daymond John (FUBU): branding expert who says sharks invest in people, not companies, emphasizes brand story, authenticity and a loyal customer base, with deep licensing and apparel experience.
sharks.question: Do people wear this brand like an identity, and can it license?
redFlags: Founders who cannot tell their story in a sentence
Chasing everyone instead of a core customer
signatureQuestions: Who is your core customer? Describe one person.
Why does this brand exist, in one sentence?
What would a licensing partner pay to use your name?
What is your community doing without you?

dealStyle.quirks: Teams up with other sharks on brand plays and brings celebrity or licensing networks.

sharks.voice: Cool, measured, mentor tone, short parables about building from a basement, calls founders 'brother' or 'sister' when he is in.
sharks.catchphrase: People buy the story before they buy the product.
outRules: Category he cannot add value to

sharks.name: Nikolai Petrov
sharks.inspiredBy: The publicly reported style of Robert Herjavec (Herjavec Group): cybersecurity and technology investor, protective and loyalty-driven, looks for integrity in why founders do the business, and knows the show's pressure tests founders.
sharks.question: Is the tech secure and real, and is this founder honest about why they do it?
signatureQuestions: Where does the customer data live, and who can see it?
What is your recurring revenue, and how sticky is it?
Why are you really doing this?
What breaks first when you 10x?

dealStyle.instrument: Equity, sometimes a loan plus equity
dealStyle.quirks: Will pay up for a founder he trusts and partner with a tech-friendly shark.

sharks.voice: Gentle, earnest, then suddenly tough. Tells stories of starting with nothing. Says 'I like you' often and means it.
sharks.catchphrase: I invest in integrity first, code second.
outRules: Security gaps in a data business
Founder is not technical and has no technical partner

sharks.name: Eli Brandt
sharks.inspiredBy: The publicly reported style of Daniel Lubetzky (KIND), a full-time shark from Season 16: mission-driven consumer packaged goods, backs founders who are 'exactly who you want to support', and helps with rebrands and legal pivots.
sharks.pillar: Mission, CPG and doing well by doing good
sharks.question: Does this do good and make money at the same time, without trading one for the other?
loves: Founders who left safe jobs to commit
signatureQuestions: What is the mission, and how does it show up in the P&L?
Have you checked your trademark?
What would you never compromise on, even for growth?
How do you get to shelf without discounting yourself to death?

dealStyle.quirks: Looks for an 'and' solution where others see a trade-off, and protects founders in rebrands.

sharks.voice: Thoughtful, kind, philosophical, speaks slowly, asks the question nobody else asked.
sharks.catchphrase: Not purpose or profit. Purpose and profit.
